chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Islam is built upon five: Wilayah, Salat, Zakat, fasting of the month of Ramadan, and Hajj.
ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars of Islam in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Al-Kafi highlights the Shia distinctiveness of placing Wilayah (divine guardianship) as the foundational pillar, preceding the ritual acts of prayer, fasting, alms-giving, and pilgrimage. This ordering underscores the theological principle that correct practice (Ibadah) is contingent upon recognizing divine authority (Imamate), a key differentiator from Sunni traditions which typically list Shahada first. The hadith thus serves as a cornerstone for understanding the integration of creed and worship in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Musna Al hannat, from Abdullah Bin Ajlan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Al-Islām is built upon five – The Wilayah, and the Salāt, and the Zakāt, and the Soām (Fast) of the Month of Ramazan, and the Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Muthanna al-Hannat from ‘Abd Allah ‘Ajlan from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
Islam is based on five principles. They are al-Wilayah, (accepting the Divine Authority of ‘ A’immah ), the prayer, al- Zakat (charity), fasting in the month of Ramadan and al-Hajj.’”
